mechanism_narrative: A higher level of residential fixed investment (RSAFS) is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as strong consumer demand supports corporate earnings growth and reduces recession risk.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where RSAFS is above its 5-year median, or the rank correlation between RSAFS and 20-day returns is negative (Rank IC < -0.03) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 4.5%, the S&P 500 produces negative forward returns over the next 5 trading days due to immediate market reactions to restrictive monetary policy.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 40% of instances, or the rank correlation between FEDFUNDS and 5-day returns is positive (Rank IC > 0.03) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 300 and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 4.0%, the S&P 500 produces negative forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to sustained monetary tightening and inflationary pressures suppressing equity valuations.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL > 300 and FEDFUNDS > 4.0%, the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances, or the rank correlation between the interaction signal and 60-day returns is positive (Rank IC > 0.03) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In periods of low unemployment (UNRATE < 4.0%), the S&P 500 produces positive forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to sustained consumer spending and corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: In periods where UNRATE < 4.0%, the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances, or the rank correlation between UNRATE and 20-day returns is negative (Rank IC < -0.03) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 100, the S&P 500 produces negative forward returns over the next 5 trading days due to immediate market concerns about economic contraction.
failure_condition: When INDPRO < 100, the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 40% of instances, or the rank correlation between INDPRO and 5-day returns is positive (Rank IC > 0.03) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, as elevated inflation erodes real earnings and increases monetary policy tightening risk.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL is above its 5-year median, or the rank correlation between CPIAUCSL and 60-day returns is positive (Rank IC > 0.03) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When residential construction activity (HOUST) exceeds 1400 and industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 100, the S&P 500 produces negative forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to conflicting demand and supply signals that increase inflationary pressure and market uncertainty.
failure_condition: When HOUST > 1400 and INDPRO < 100, the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances, or the rank correlation between the interaction signal and 20-day returns is positive (Rank IC > 0.03) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of active monetary tightening (FEDFUNDS rising > 0.2% over 3 months), the S&P 500 produces negative forward returns over the next 5 trading days due to immediate market reactions to tightening policy.
failure_condition: During periods of active monetary tightening (FEDFUNDS rising > 0.2% over 3 months), the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 40% of instances, or the rank correlation between the tightening signal and 5-day returns is positive (Rank IC > 0.03) over any 3-year rolling window.
